papers.title_en: MoPrO-SD: Modular Prompt Optimization for Stance Detection
papers.authors: Meysam Sabbaghan, Nikesh Gyawali, Arman Zareian Jahromi, Sebastian Loera-Lozano, Doina Caragea, Cornelia Caragea
papers.evidence: 模块化提示词优化框架
papers.tldr: 针对大模型在立场检测中面临的隐晦表达和讽刺等挑战，本文提出了MoPrO-SD框架。该方法通过将提示词分解为功能性语义模块，并利用基于类条件反馈的LLM进行序列化优化。研究引入了VaccineStance数据集，实验表明该方法在多个数据集和模型上均优于人工编写的基准提示词，有效提升了立场检测的准确性。
papers.abstract_en: Stance detection remains challenging for large language models (LLMs) due to implicit opinions, sarcasm, and context-dependent expressions of stance. Although automatic prompt optimization offers an alternative to fine-tuning without updating model parameters, existing structured approaches are not specifically designed around stance-label semantics and class-specific ambiguities. We introduce MoPrO-SD, a stance-specific prompt optimization framework that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules and refines them sequentially using LLM-based feedback. We study three refinement strategies: instruction-only optimization (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), and instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E), using class-conditioned errors for stance-label refinement. We also introduce VaccineStance, a new human-annotated benchmark for vaccine stance detection. Experiments across four datasets and five open-weight LLMs show that MoPrO-SD improves upon the human-written Base prompt in many settings. On SemEval-2016, class-conditioned feedback achieves higher mean Macro-F1 than pooled feedback for four of five backbones. Both reasoning-based strategies, I+R and I+R+E, achieve strong performance, with their relative effectiveness varying across models and datasets, while remaining competitive with recent prompt optimization methods. The MoPrO-SD code and VaccineStance dataset are available on GitHub.

papers.title_en: Reflective Prompt Optimization of a Deep-Research Agent: A Topic-Disjoint, Multi-Seed Protocol for Measuring Transferable Gains and Prompt-Level Overfitting
papers.authors: Elias Lumer, Sahil Sen, Vamse Kumar Subbiah, Kevin Paul
papers.evidence: 针对多智能体深度研究代理的反射式提示词演化 (GEPA)
papers.tldr: 本文研究了深度研究智能体中提示词优化（Prompt Optimization）的过拟合风险。作者提出了一种基于主题隔离和多随机种子的评估协议，通过反射式提示进化（GEPA）优化系统提示词。研究发现，尽管提示词中存在类似“记忆”的片段，但性能提升主要源于分解式反馈机制而非死记硬背。该工作为提示词优化提供了更严谨的评估框架，并证明了多维度反馈对模型泛化能力的关键作用。
papers.abstract_en: Prompt optimization is an attractive alternative to reinforcement learning for adapting language-model agents, since it is cheap and produces human-readable artifacts. On factual tasks, however, it carries a failure mode that scalar-reward reinforcement learning does not. An optimizer that reads the training examples can write their answers into the prompt, so an in-distribution gain may be memorization rather than transferable behaviour. We apply reflective prompt evolution (GEPA) to the two system prompts of a multi-agent deep-research agent and evaluate it under a topic-disjoint split in which no topic is shared across train, validation, and test. Held-out citation reward rises by 0.079, from 0.702 to 0.781, with a bootstrap 95\% confidence interval of [0.051, 0.107], and the gain replicates across three seeds (mean 0.107). Nearly half of the winning prompt is a memorized answer key, yet a controlled ablation shows this content earns no reward even on the exact training questions it encodes. The large validation-minus-held-out gap is therefore small-sample selection under a noisy judge, not memorization. Varying the verifier isolates what makes the gain transfer. Decomposed per-dimension feedback is the causal ingredient, and collapsing it to a single scalar reward makes held-out transfer negative. The gain persists under an out-of-family judge and is largely reproduced by a hand-written version of the discovered recipe. Credible evaluation of prompt optimizers therefore requires held-out topics, multiple seeds, and verifier ablations. We release the candidate prompts, lineage diffs, figures, tables, and analysis.

papers.title_en: Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization via Zeroth-Order Residual Tracking
papers.authors: El Mahdi Chayti, Alireza Mirrokni, Martin Jaggi
papers.evidence: 具有黑盒下层问题的双层优化
papers.tldr: 针对仅能获取部分梯度信息的优化问题，本文提出了部分信息随机优化（PISO）算法。该方法通过结合已知梯度分量与残差的动态估计，利用零阶残差跟踪技术降低随机探测带来的方差。PISO在非凸优化中实现了收敛保证，并在性能预测、强化学习及双层优化任务中展现了优于现有零阶优化方法的效率与性能。
papers.abstract_en: Many optimization problems provide direct access to only part of the gradient, while the remaining component must be inferred from function evaluations. This structure arises in performative prediction, performative reinforcement learning, and bilevel optimization with a black-box lower level. We introduce Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization (PISO), which combines the available gradient component with a running estimate of the residual. By centring each zeroth-order observation on this estimate, PISO makes the variance due to random probing depend on the tracking error rather than the residual's magnitude. This yields a randomized sketch iteration with an explicit contraction mechanism and a principled interpretation of momentum. For smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence guarantees that depend on the residual's variation and initial magnitude, without requiring a uniform bound on the unavailable gradient component. With independently sampled function evaluations and Gaussian or spherical probes, PISO attains leading function-evaluation complexities of \(O(d^{2}\varepsilon^{-6})\) under Lipschitz gradients and \(O(d^{2}\varepsilon^{-5})\) under an additional Lipschitz-Hessian assumption. These rates require only one probe direction, two function samples, and one known-component sample per update. The analysis also quantifies how batching trades observations for fewer deployments. Across five settings, PISO variants improve on the tested baselines with comparable oracle access in three, reach a comparable solution faster in bilevel routing, and perform best among methods without response-model derivatives in performative reinforcement learning.

papers.title_en: TraceICL: Thread-Resolved Demonstration Curation with Consistency Calibration for Robust Multimodal In-Context Learning
papers.authors: Yigit Yilmaz, Elena Petrova, Mehmet Kaya, Lucia Rossi, Amir Rahman
papers.evidence: 自动化的上下文学习示例策划
papers.tldr: 针对多模态上下文学习（ICL）中存在的图像文本绑定错误、冗余示例干扰及噪声答案误导问题，本文提出了无需训练的框架AVA。该框架通过线程分解、影响力驱动的选择策略以及弱到强的置信度校准，有效提升了冻结大视觉语言模型（LVLM）在多模态任务中的鲁棒性与准确性，在多个基准测试中显著优于现有基线。
papers.abstract_en: Interleaved multimodal in-context learning (ICL) lets frozen large vision-language models (LVLMs) acquire new tasks from a handful of image-text-answer demonstrations, yet it remains fragile: demonstrations bind to the wrong images, redundant exemplars crowd out informative ones, and noisy answers are copied verbatim into predictions. We present AVA, a training-free framework that organizes the demonstration pipeline of multimodal ICL into three composable stages. A Thread-Resolved Decomposer (TRD) segments the interleaved context into per-sample threads and re-stitches them with explicit boundaries, restoring image-text binding. An Influence-scored Demonstration Selector (IDS) estimates each candidate's marginal influence with one extra forward pass, removes redundancy, and orders the survivors by descending value. A Weak-to-Strong Consistency Calibration (WSC) module scores each demonstration by a weak sibling model's reconstruction confidence and softly reweights its contribution during decoding. On five vision-language benchmarks with interleaved 4-shot prompts, AVA improves the strongest same-setting baseline by +1.7 points on average, with gains of up to +2.4 points on VizWiz, shrinks the require-visual performance gap on ScienceQA-IMG, and retains most of its gain under 30% noisy demonstrations, at a 26% latency overhead that an offline cache amortizes. No gradients are ever computed; the LVLM stays frozen.

papers.title_en: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention
papers.authors: Zhiqiang Pang, Zihong Sun, Qi Xie, Jun Shu, Deyu Meng, Zongben Xu
papers.evidence: 用于高效参数适配的分层选择性微调
papers.tldr: 本文针对大模型微调中“任务适配与通用能力保持”的权衡问题，提出了一种基于层选择的微调策略。研究发现不同Transformer层对任务的敏感度不同，通过引入输入输出余弦相似度作为轻量级指标，识别并仅在敏感层部署LoRA适配器（LS-LoRA），在提升目标任务性能的同时，显著减少了通用能力的退化。
papers.abstract_en: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables large language models (LLMs) to adapt to specialized tasks, but often at the cost of degrading general capabilities acquired during pretraining. Existing approaches primarily mitigate this trade-off through data replay or regularization, relying on additional data or explicit optimization constraints. We instead focus on a different question: where should adaptation be applied? We find that fine-tuning different Transformer layers produces different target-task gains and degrees of capability degradation, suggesting that not all layers are equally suitable for adaptation. To characterize this difference, we use layer-wise empirical Fisher information to measure target-task sensitivity. However, computing Fisher scores requires backward computation and becomes increasingly expensive for large models. We therefore introduce input--output cosine similarity as a lightweight, forward-only proxy for ranking layer sensitivity. Across models and tasks, layers with lower input--output similarity consistently exhibit higher empirical Fisher scores. Building on this observation, we propose Layer-Selective LoRA (LS-LoRA), which places trainable LoRA adapters only in layers with low input--output similarity. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation show that LS-LoRA improves average target-task performance while retaining substantially more commonsense reasoning capability than standard all-layer LoRA, demonstrating that carefully choosing where to adapt can provide a simple and effective way to balance target-task adaptation and general capability retention.

papers.title_en: SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection
papers.authors: Ziyu Luo, Wei Li, Haoping Huang, Kecheng Liu, Min Gao
papers.evidence: 结合软硬提示的大语言模型引导数据增强
papers.tldr: 针对低资源环境下虚假新闻检测数据稀缺及难以捕捉细微欺骗模式的问题，本文提出了SharP框架。该方法利用大语言模型（LLM），通过软硬提示词结合及边界感知策略生成高质量、任务相关的合成样本，有效提升了分类器在低资源场景下的鲁棒性与泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: Fake news detection under low resource conditions is challenged by the scarcity of labeled data and the difficulty of capturing subtle deceptive patterns. In this work, we focus on low resource fake news detection, where only a small labeled set is available for training, while evaluation is performed under a fixed and unchanged test protocol. This setting is motivated by costly, ambiguous fact-checking and emerging topics and domains that are poorly covered by existing benchmarks. Existing data augmentation methods, such as synonym substitution, generative adversarial networks, and large language model (LLM)-based generation, often produce fluent but overly generic content, lacking the task-specific relevance needed for accurate detection. To address this, we propose SharP, a boundary-aware text generation framework guided by soft and hard prompts, which leverages LLMs as tools adapted to produce task-specific synthetic samples. SharP employs a dual prompt mechanism: hard prompts provide structured guidance and factual constraints, while soft prompts introduce learned semantic patterns from the data. These two types of prompts are combined to guide the generation process, enabling the model to produce samples that closely align with the characteristics of news. To further enhance detection performance, we incorporate a boundary-aware strategy that steers generation toward areas where the classifier is less confident, helping to clarify subtle distinctions between real and fake content. In addition, we adopt a dual objective optimization that balances semantic alignment with the source data and classifier feedback. This encourages the generation of samples that are both domain-consistent and helpful for refining decision boundaries, ultimately improving model robustness and generalization in low resource fake news detection.

papers.title_en: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
papers.authors: Jiwon Jeon, Myungsik Cho, Jeonghye Kim, Youngchul Sung
papers.evidence: 学习在何处注入用户提示以进行大模型自我纠错
papers.tldr: 针对大模型自我纠错能力不足的问题，本文提出UPTURN框架。该方法无需微调模型，通过训练一个轻量级MLP头识别推理失败的干预点，并以“新用户轮次”而非“插入Token”的方式注入纠错指令，从而有效引导模型修正推理路径。实验表明，UPTURN在多个数学基准测试中显著提升了模型准确率，且具有良好的跨模型迁移能力。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.
